item.title: Sigatoka farmer claims his three-acre pawpaw farm was deliberately set on fire
item.description: A Sigatoka farmer is appealing for help after his three-acre pawpaw farm was set on fire last Saturday, leaving him worried about how he will support his young family and recover from the losses. Mohit Kumar says he suffered losses estimated at between $5,000 and $6,000 following the fire.
item.content:encoded:
A Sigatoka farmer is appealing for help after his three-acre pawpaw farm was set on fire last Saturday, leaving him worried about how he will support his young family and recover from the losses.

Mohit Kumar says he suffered losses estimated at between $5,000 and $6,000 following the fire.

He says he has been in the farming business for 30 years, and this is the first time he has experienced an incident like this.

Insert: Kumar on his source of income 9th Nov

Speaking to fijivillage News, Kumar says he was alerted about the fire by a neighbour, but by the time he reached the farm, it was too late to control the blaze.

Kumar , who is renting the land, says he is particularly worried about supporting his young children, who are attending school.

He claims that a group of boys have been drinking alcohol on his farm f or the past two to three years and believes they may have started the fire while intoxicated.

Kumar says he is not blaming anyone directly, but found beer bottles and cans scattered around the farm after the fire.

He says the issue of people drinking on farms has been ongoing and had been reported previously.

Kumar is calling on Police to conduct regular patrols along Valley Road and surrounding farms, saying people often gather there to drink alcohol.

He is also appealing to the Government for assistance through subsidised seedlings or other support to help him re-establish his farm.

Kumar says rebuilding his livelihood will be particularly difficult amid the El Niño conditions.

item.title: Teachers raise student safety concerns at Suva Bus Stand
item.description: Teachers are calling for stronger measures to be implemented to ensure students return home safely after school, raising concerns about children spending extended periods at the Suva Bus Stand. The issue was raised during a public consultation on the Education Act in Lami, where a teacher expressed concern about students spending a long time at the bus stand instead of boarding their buses and tra
item.content:encoded:
Teachers are calling for stronger measures to be implemented to ensure students return home safely after school, raising concerns about children spending extended periods at the Suva Bus Stand.

The issue was raised during a public consultation on the Education Act in Lami, where a teacher expressed concern about students spending a long time at the bus stand instead of boarding their buses and travelling home.

The teacher says Suva City Council officers regularly make announcements over the PA system, reminding students to board their buses and leave the area.

He says students could be exposed to social problems while spending extended periods at the bus stand, and believes stronger measures should be considered to protect their safety.

However, the teacher acknowledges that some students may be facing transport difficulties, which could explain why they remain at the bus stand after school.

Another teacher suggested reintroducing dedicated school buses to transport students directly between their schools and homes.

The teacher says this could reduce the number of students spending time at bus stands and provide safer transport arrangements.

Responding to the concerns, the Ministry of Education representative says students safety is a shared responsibility between the Ministry, teachers and parents.

He says parents must remind their children to travel directly home after school rather than remaining in town longer than necessary.

He also acknowledges teachers who go beyond their normal duties to help supervise students at bus stands.

He says the Ministry has heard the concerns and will look into the issue, including holding discussions with transport service providers.

He explains that students receiving transport assistance are registered to use specific bus services through their bus cards.

He stresses that parents have an important role in ensuring their children travel safely between school and home.

item.title: Afroz Ali remanded over alleged sacrilege cases in Ba
item.description: 33-year-old Afroz Ali, who is charged in connection with a series of alleged sacrilege cases in Ba has been remanded in custody. Ali, who is from Varavu in B a, appeared in a special court sitting in the Ba Magistrates Court today.
item.content:encoded:
33-year-old Afroz Ali, who is charged in connection with a series of alleged sacrilege cases in Ba has been remanded in custody.

Ali, who is from Varavu in B a, appeared in a special court sitting in the Ba Magistrates Court today.

He is charged with three counts of sacrilege and six counts of breach of order of suspended sentence.

Ali is alleged to have unlawfully entered three temples and stole religious statues, which were later found damaged.

One of the incidents allegedly occurred at a temple in Rarawai on 5th November, where the accused is alleged to have stolen a religious statue.

The statue was later found in pieces in a nearby creek.

The case will be called again on the 30th of this month.

item.title: Around 60 elderly people and persons with disabilities celebrate Diwali at Valelevu Nursing Home
item.description: Around 60 elderly people and persons living with disabilities came together to celebrate Diwali at the Valelevu Nursing Home, in an event aimed at promoting inclusion, fellowship and community support. The celebration was organised by the Nasinu Older Persons Association in partnership with the Caubati Youth Ramayan Mandli under the theme “Empowering Elderly Through Divine Worship”.
item.content:encoded:
Around 60 elderly people and persons living with disabilities came together to celebrate Diwali at the Valelevu Nursing Home, in an event aimed at promoting inclusion, fellowship and community support.

The celebration was organised by the Nasinu Older Persons Association in partnership with the Caubati Youth Ramayan Mandli under the theme “Empowering Elderly Through Divine Worship”.

The event was attended by the Vice President of Sanatan Dharam Fiji, Virendra Lal, who was the chief guest, as well as the CEO of HART Fiji and representatives from the Nasinu Welfare Office.

In his Diwali message, Nasinu Older Persons Association Chair and Trustee Randhir Prasad highlighted that Diwali represents the victory of light over darkness, knowledge over ignorance and hope over adversity.

Prasad says the festival brings people together and reminds everyone of the importance of family, friendship and community.

He also encouraged people to show empathy, work together and support one another.

Prasad highlighted the association's commitment to protecting older persons from abuse and supporting their wellbeing through community awareness programmes, celebrations and home visits.

Meanwhile, the CEO of HART Fiji acknowledged the support and contributions of organisations such as the Nasinu Older Persons Association in caring for and supporting members of the community.

The celebration provided an opportunity for elderly people and persons living with disabilities to share in the spirit of Diwali and strengthen their sense of belonging and connection with the community.

item.title: Conjoined twins recovering well after successful separation in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The mother of the conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe who were successfully separated in Saudi Arabia, says she is overjoyed to see her babies recovering well after the operation, describing the moment they were separated as precious. Speaking to fijivillage News, Tacaqe says the twins spent five days in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit before being transferred to the general ward.
item.content:encoded:
The mother of the conjoined twins, Akeneta Rokobati Tacaqe who were successfully separated in Saudi Arabia, says she is overjoyed to see her babies recovering well after the operation, describing the moment they were separated as precious.

Speaking to fijivillage News, Tacaqe says the twins spent five days in the Paediatric Intensive Care Unit before being transferred to the general ward.

She says the babies were initially placed in separate rooms before doctors moved them into one room two days later.

Tacaqe says the twins no longer require oxygen, are breathing well and have started taking food after being on milk for a few days.

She says the family had been waiting for this moment for several months and were initially nervous while watching the operation live, but later became more comfortable.

Tacaqe says she is particularly happy to see her babies separated and thanked the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for making the operation possible.

She says the family wanted to give twinsÂ Jesipeli and Di Cecea Kikau Â an additional Arabic name Sara and Noura as a way of showing their appreciation to Saudi Arabia for what it has done for them.

Tacaqe also praised the medical staff for their expertise, care and kindness, saying they looked after the family very well throughout their hospital stay.

She says the support from families in Saudi Arabia who regularly visit them has also made them feel at home away from home.

Tacaqe says her family back home is overjoyed and cannot wait to meet the babies.

She hopes to bring the twins back to Saudi Arabia one day to show them where they were separated.

She also hopes the children may one day consider working in the medical field as doctors or nurses so they can give back to the community and help others.

Tacaqe thanked everyone who has kept her family in their thoughts and prayers, saying the babies are doing well and their return to Fiji has not yet been decided as they are still recovering.

item.title: Drains are not rubbish bins – Nasinu Town Council
item.description: The Nasinu Town Council is urging residents and businesses to stop dumping rubbish into drains, warning that blockages can cause flooding and create unhealthy living conditions during heavy rain. The Council says its operations team is carrying out drain-cleaning work across different wards in Nasinu, removing rubbish, debris and other materials obstructing water flow.
item.content:encoded:
The Nasinu Town Council is urging residents and businesses to stop dumping rubbish into drains, warning that blockages can cause flooding and create unhealthy living conditions during heavy rain.

The Council says its operations team is carrying out drain-cleaning work across different wards in Nasinu, removing rubbish, debris and other materials obstructing water flow.

The Council says blocked drains can lead to flooding, stagnant water, unpleasant odours and unhealthy conditions for families living nearby.

Residents are being reminded that drains are not rubbish bins and should not be used to dispose of household waste, plastics, bottles or grass cuttings.

The Council says while its workers continue clearing drains, residents and businesses must also take responsibility by disposing of their rubbish properly.

The Council stresses that keeping communities clean and safe is everyone's responsibility.

The Nasinu Town Council is encouraging everyone to work together to keep drains clear, maintain a clean environment and reduce the risk of flooding during heavy rain.
